fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Storage Area; Storage Area; Equipment Storage Area; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Access Drive
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions of approach.
• Mark the detached structure with a separate address or unit identifier so responders can quickly distinguish it from the main residence.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Trim any trees or shrubs overhanging the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for fire apparatus and ladder trucks.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of parked vehicles, stored equipment, and debris to allow a responding vehicle to reach both structures without stopping.
• Designate and mark a turnaround area near the end of the access drive so responding vehicles are not required to back out onto the road.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• Store equipment and materials inside the equipment storage area rather than in front of or beside it, so the surrounding ground remains clear for responder movement.
• Keep the storage areas clear of stacked materials that would block access to the sides or rear of either structure.
• Post a simple site diagram at the driveway entrance showing the location of both structures, the storage areas, and the access drive layout.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Wood Piles; Adequate Vegetation Separation; None Visible
wildfire.recommendations:
• Move wood piles away from the structure and store them at least 30 feet from any building.
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees close to the structure to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Remove shrubs growing directly beneath or immediately next to any scattered trees near the structure.
• Keep the open terrain areas between the structure and tree clusters free of dry grass, dead leaves, and fallen branches.
